name: Solace Arid
geological_features: Dry salt flats spanning hundreds of kilometers
Deep arroyos from extinct river systems
specific_features: Perfectly preserved fossil dunes of compressed iron-oxide sand
A colossal natural stone arch bridging a canyon over forty kilometers wide
description: Solace Arid is a medium-sized desert world of austere, wind-sculpted beauty. Towering mesas of layered sandstone rise above vast salt flats, and deep arroyos cut through the terrain like the memory of rivers that dried up ages ago.

The thin atmosphere bleeds heat rapidly after sunset, creating punishing temperature swings between day and night. Winds carry fine iron-oxide dust that tints the sky a permanent shade of pale rust, and visibility during the frequent dust devils can drop to near zero.

There is no evidence that Solace Arid ever supported life, though its extinct river systems suggest a wetter epoch in the deep geological past. What cataclysm robbed the planet of its water remains unclear -- theories range from solar evolution to a slow atmospheric loss through the thin magnetosphere.

The planet's stark landscapes and mineral-rich terrain have drawn interest from both surveyors and frontier settlers seeking isolation. Its abundant solar exposure and accessible silicon deposits make it a viable candidate for solar infrastructure development, provided the dust can be managed.
